The serde_json json! macro generates code that relies on the serde_json::to_value function and its associated unwrap calls to convert interpolated expressions into Value objects [1][2]. Because Path and PathBuf in Rust may contain non-UTF-8 data (as they represent OS-specific paths), they cannot be serialized directly to a standard UTF-8 JSON string [3][4]. Attempting to serialize such a path typically results in a serialization error [3]. 2. Macro behavior: If you attempt to use the json! macro with an object that fails to serialize (such as a PathBuf containing invalid UTF-8), the call to to_value inside the macro will return an Err, and the subsequent.unwrap will cause your program to panic [1][3]. 3. Common strategies include using #[serde(with = "...")] to serialize the PathBuf as a sequence of bytes (Vec<u8>) or converting it to an OsString/OsStr before serialization, though the latter can lead to platform-specific portability issues [4]. In summary, the json! macro is not suitable for handling data structures that may fail to serialize, such as paths containing arbitrary non-UTF-8 byte sequences, because its internal use of unwrap treats any serialization error as a fatal panic [1][3].

<excerpt>While testing this simple schema, I was lulled into a false sense of security by `serde_json` providing a serializer for `PathBuf` by default. #[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "lowercase")] pub enum Entry { File { path: PathBuf, inode: Option, size: u64, modified: Option // FIXME: Work around serde_json bug `#464` }, Directory { path: PathBuf, inode: Option, modified: Option // FIXME: Work around serde_json bug `#464` }, Symlink { path: PathBuf, target: Option }, Unknown { path: PathBuf } } Specifically, when I moved on to more thorough testing, serialization failed with this message: error: serialization failure caused by: path contains invalid UTF-8 characters Wallpapering over the fundamental point to *having* a distinction between `String` and `OsString` (which `PathBuf` wraps) in this "do what I mean and hope it doesn&`#39`;t break" sort of way feels more like what I&`#39`;d expect of a serializer for a weakly typed language, like Perl or PHP, rather than a "Strongly typed JSON library for Rust", which makes for a big footgun. If you&`#39`;re unwilling to be opinionated about how to escape/encode arbitrary bytestrings (POSIX) or un-paired UTF-16 surrogates (Windows) into UTF-8 for storage in JSON, I&`#39`;d much prefer serde_json to take inspiration from `Result` and force me to explicitly choose a resolution strategy before my code will compile.
